Cells of a burn as polygons in world coordinates

Source: R/cb_affine.R
cb_cells.Rd

One quadrilateral per record cell, in the grid's world coordinates: the cells of every run expanded, then the edge, line and point cells. For a burn from cb_burn_index() the quadrilaterals are rotated or sheared as the grid is; for a regular cb_burn() they are rectangles. Intended for plotting (ggplot2::geom_polygon()) and for export.

Usage

cb_cells(x, max_cells = 1e+05)

Arguments

x

A cb_burn object.

max_cells

Refuse to build more cells than this (runs can cover very many cells), to avoid exhausting memory by accident.

Value

A data frame with four rows per cell and columns cell (cell number, the polygon group), x, y (the corner, in order around the cell), row, col, id, kind (run, edge, line or point) and value (1 for runs and points, the coverage fraction for edges, the length for lines).

Examples

b <- cb_burn(wk::wkt("POLYGON ((1.5 1.5, 4.5 1.5, 4.5 3.5, 1.5 1.5))"),
             extent = c(0, 6, 0, 5), dimension = c(6, 5))
head(cb_cells(b), 8)
#>   cell x y row col id kind      value
#> 1    1 3 4   2   4  1 edge 0.02083333
#> 2    1 4 4   2   4  1 edge 0.02083333
#> 3    1 4 3   2   4  1 edge 0.02083333
#> 4    1 3 3   2   4  1 edge 0.02083333
#> 5    2 4 4   2   5  1 edge 0.16666667
#> 6    2 5 4   2   5  1 edge 0.16666667
#> 7    2 5 3   2   5  1 edge 0.16666667
#> 8    2 4 3   2   5  1 edge 0.16666667
